Requests.ProblemText: We want to understand why some college students choose not to attend professor office hours.
Our company wants to know what percentage of customers prefer online shopping over shopping in person.
We want to determine whether a new tutoring program improves students' exam scores compared with students who do not use it.
We want to understand how people's attitudes toward remote work change over a five-year period.
Our city is considering a ban on single-use plastic bags. We want to understand how similar policies have affected waste in other cities.
We want to learn what teenagers think makes a social media app enjoyable to use.
We have developed a prototype water bottle and want to test different lid designs to determine which is easiest to use.
Scientists want to better understand how a newly discovered protein interacts with human cells without developing an immediate commercial application.
We want to observe how customers actually move through our grocery store and which displays they stop at.
We want to determine whether students who sleep at least eight hours tend to have higher GPAs.
Our hospital wants to combine patient surveys with interviews to understand why patients miss scheduled appointments.
We want to combine the results of existing published studies to determine whether meditation reduces stress.
We don't know why users are abandoning our mobile application during account creation and want to investigate possible reasons.
A school wants to determine whether providing free breakfast improves student attendance.
Our company wants to know whether customers would be interested in buying a cheaper version of our current product.
We want to interview first-generation college students about the challenges they experience during their first semester.
We want to track the same group of graduates for ten years to see how their careers develop.
A state recently changed its minimum wage. We want to examine how the change affected employment and local businesses.
We want to test whether changing the color of a website's checkout button increases the percentage of visitors who complete a purchase.
Engineers want to investigate the fundamental properties of a new material before deciding what products it might be useful for.
We want researchers to spend time inside several classrooms observing how teachers and students use tablets during normal lessons.
We want to measure customer satisfaction numerically using a survey sent to 5,000 customers.
We want to understand both how many students use campus mental-health resources and what experiences students have when using them.
We are designing a new mobile application and want to repeatedly build and test prototypes with potential users.
We want to examine all high-quality published research comparing remote learning with classroom learning.
A restaurant wants to understand which new menu items its target customers would be most likely to purchase.
We have noticed employees leaving our company more frequently, but we don't know why and want to identify possible explanations.
A factory wants to determine whether a new workflow can reduce the average time required to assemble a product.
We want to study how residents actually use a newly constructed public park during different times of day.
We want to follow children from elementary school through high school to study how reading habits develop as they age.
The university is considering changing its parking rules. We want to investigate how the proposed policy could affect students and employees.
We want to collect numerical pollution measurements and interview residents to understand both pollution levels and how residents believe pollution affects their neighborhood.
We want to determine whether people assigned to use a new study technique perform better on a memory test than people assigned to use their normal technique.
Our engineering team wants to create and test several versions of a low-cost air-quality sensor before choosing a final design.
Which video game is objectively the greatest video game ever made?
We need researchers to prove that our company's product is better than every competitor's product, regardless of what the evidence shows.
Can you tell us exactly what the stock market will be worth twenty years from today?
We want a study proving that our CEO is the best CEO in the country, regardless of what the evidence shows.
Can researchers determine whether pineapple belongs on pizza once and for all?
We want to know the exact thoughts every American will have about artificial intelligence ten years from now.
